scenes.visual: Hook before the title. Reuse chapter one's map: blue observed labels and tracers; gold time; green inherited mark or reporter; red intervention or deletion; grey unobserved cells and DNA. A green family tree from chapter one stands beside one red gene block locked inside a grey cell. On-screen label: schematic.

scenes.tts: Chapter one asked what a label can prove. How can we test what a gene does in one cell type, after birth? We need to control three things: the target, the place, and the time.
scenes.visual: Carry chapter one's green family tree into the left third. On the right, reveal three large controls around the red gene block: target brackets, a cell-type gate, and a gold clock. Each control turns from a question mark into an empty slot.
scenes.narration: Chapter one asked what a label can prove. How can we test what a gene does in one cell type, after birth? We need to control three things: the target, the place, and the time.

scenes.visual: Brief title over the carried family tree and three control slots: Build a Conditional Test.

scenes.tts: First, build the target. Place lox P sites around an important gene segment. This floxed allele is designed to work normally until Cree recombinase removes that segment. A Cree-free control must test whether the allele really does work normally.
scenes.caption: First, build the target. Place loxP sites around an important gene segment. This floxed allele is designed to work normally until Cre recombinase removes that segment. A Cre-free control must test whether the allele really does work normally.
scenes.visual: Zoom into a grey DNA bar. Two red vertical brackets settle around one red labelled block. Before Cre, an output gauge carries a question mark. A separate Cre-free control bar moves underneath; only a measured control result changes both gauges to working. No molecular structure is drawn.
scenes.narration: First, build the target. Place loxP sites around an important gene segment. This floxed allele is designed to work normally until Cre recombinase removes that segment. A Cre-free control must test whether the allele really does work normally.

scenes.tts: Next, control the place. A cell-type promoter supplies Cree only where that driver is active. Cree deletes the bracketed segment largely in those cells. But a driver's actual range and completeness must be measured, not assumed from its name.
scenes.caption: Next, control the place. A cell-type promoter supplies Cre only where that driver is active. Cre deletes the bracketed segment largely in those cells. But a driver's actual range and completeness must be measured, not assumed from its name.
scenes.visual: Show six grey cells in a tissue. A red driver gate opens in three. A red Cre intervention token enters those cells and removes the bracketed block. One intended cell stays unrecombined, and one neighbouring cell recombines, illustrating mosaic and off-target patterns without claiming frequency.
scenes.narration: Next, control the place. A cell-type promoter supplies Cre only where that driver is active. Cre deletes the bracketed segment largely in those cells. But a driver's actual range and completeness must be measured, not assumed from its name.

scenes.tts: Then control the time. Cree E R is designed to keep Cree outside the nucleus until tamoxifen is given. A gold time gate opens after birth. Recombination is concentrated after dosing, but its actual timing must be measured.
scenes.caption: Then control the time. CreER is designed to keep Cre outside the nucleus until tamoxifen is given. A gold time gate opens after birth. Recombination is concentrated after dosing, but its actual timing must be measured.
scenes.visual: Carry one target cell onto a gold before-and-after timeline. Before tamoxifen, most red Cre tokens wait outside a grey nucleus beside a small timing question mark. At the gold dose marker, the gate opens; Cre enters and the red target block disappears.
scenes.narration: Then control the time. CreER is designed to keep Cre outside the nucleus until tamoxifen is given. A gold time gate opens after birth. Recombination is concentrated after dosing, but its actual timing must be measured.

scenes.tts: Now read the cross one locus at a time. Avil Cree over plus supplies one Cree driver allele. Trk A floxed over minus supplies one floxed allele and one null allele. The semicolon joins the two instructions in one mouse.
scenes.caption: Now read the cross one locus at a time. AvilCre/+ supplies one Cre driver allele. TrkAfl/− supplies one floxed allele and one null allele. The semicolon joins the two instructions in one mouse.
scenes.visual: Split a large genotype card at its semicolon. The left red card becomes one driver allele plus one non-Cre allele. The right grey card holds one floxed TrkA allele with a red segment plus one null allele. Rejoin the cards over the same schematic mouse.
scenes.narration: Now read the cross one locus at a time. AvilCre/+ supplies one Cre driver allele. TrkAfl/− supplies one floxed allele and one null allele. The semicolon joins the two instructions in one mouse.

scenes.tts: A matched control changes one causal piece. Keep the floxed and null Trk A alleles, but remove Cree. That mouse preserves the target genotype without triggering deletion. A second control can retain Cree while keeping one working Trk A copy.
scenes.caption: A matched control changes one causal piece. Keep the floxed and null TrkA alleles, but remove Cre. That mouse preserves the target genotype without triggering deletion. A second control can retain Cre while keeping one working TrkA copy.
scenes.visual: Duplicate the experimental mouse into two aligned rows. In row one, slide away only the red Cre card; leave both TrkA cards fixed. In row two, keep Cre and replace the null card with a working grey plus card. Highlight the single changed piece each time.
scenes.narration: A matched control changes one causal piece. Keep the floxed and null TrkA alleles, but remove Cre. That mouse preserves the target genotype without triggering deletion. A second control can retain Cre while keeping one working TrkA copy.

scenes.tts: Now predict carefully. A cell glows green from a Cree-dependent reporter. Does that glow prove the separate floxed target gene was deleted?
scenes.caption: Now predict carefully. A cell glows green from a Cre-dependent reporter. Does that glow prove the separate floxed target gene was deleted?
scenes.visual: Zoom into one green glowing cell. Place its green reporter locus on the left and its separate red floxed target locus on the right. A large question mark hangs between them. Do not show a check or cross.
scenes.narration: Now predict carefully. A cell glows green from a Cre-dependent reporter. Does that glow prove the separate floxed target gene was deleted?

scenes.visual: Thinking pause. The reporter lamp pulses gently while the separate target locus stays unchanged and unjudged. A four-and-a-half-second ring closes around the question mark.

scenes.tts: No. The reporter and target are separate lox-flanked loci, and they can recombine differently. Old target protein can also persist after deletion. Reporter light shows reporter recombination. Measure the target protein itself in those cells.
scenes.visual: Animate two independent paths. The green reporter path recombines and lights. The red target path remains a question, then gains one measurement icon labelled target protein. A faded red protein block lingers briefly after a deletion animation.
scenes.narration: No. The reporter and target are separate lox-flanked loci, and they can recombine differently. Old target protein can also persist after deletion. Reporter light shows reporter recombination. Measure the target protein itself in those cells.

scenes.tts: Only then interpret the outcome. Removing a gene tests whether it is necessary under those conditions. Imposing activity with an actuator tests whether activity is sufficient. A reporter observes a state; it does not impose that state.
scenes.visual: Build two parallel experiment lanes. In the red lane, remove a gene block and watch an outcome gauge. In a second red lane, an actuator switch drives a cell and the gauge changes. A green reporter lamp sits beside both lanes but never touches the gauge.
scenes.narration: Only then interpret the outcome. Removing a gene tests whether it is necessary under those conditions. Imposing activity with an actuator tests whether activity is sufficient. A reporter observes a state; it does not impose that state.

scenes.tts: A conditional experiment is a chain. Match the genotype to the perturbation, the perturbation to the measured readout, and the readout to the claim. Check every link with a control in practice. One weak link limits the conclusion.
scenes.visual: Arrange four large linked blocks across the frame: genotype, perturbation, readout, claim. Animate a pulse through the chain. Add a control brace beneath each link. One link thins; the pulse stops there and the final claim boundary contracts.
scenes.narration: A conditional experiment is a chain. Match the genotype to the perturbation, the perturbation to the measured readout, and the readout to the claim. Check every link with a control in practice. One weak link limits the conclusion.

scenes.visual: End card: Match the genotype, perturbation, readout and claim. Keep the four linked blocks moving slowly behind it.
